If you press W to move forward, I'm teleporting the player backwards which should look like an endless walkway. It does, with the exception of the "gun" model that streaks when the player/camera is reset. I have gone over the documentation for the past three days trying to figure out how to interpolate both the camera *and* a gun model that has additional movement (in this case some y/z positioning, but you might use weapon sway or non-animated gun bob) and doesn't streak.

Animation players seem to interpolate the movement (so some weapon bob can be added this way) but there's no way of having streak-free weapon movement controlled in code without seperately interpolating the weapon mode, which causes this disconnect and visual artifacting between the player/camera interpolation when teleporting.

- Camera has physics interpolation turned on
- Position marker has physics interpolation turned off
- Camera lerps to position marker in `lerp_cam_pos()`

- Attached weapon node has physics interpolation turned off
- Attached weapon node lerps to camera position in `weap_rotate()`

I could go back to just letting the weapon node inherit from the parent camera transform if I could figure out how to stop the streaking when adjusting the weapon position manually. Resetting the physics interpolation doesn't work as it needs to be interpolated to the parent camera, but adding weapon sway or any kinda of movement via code causes streaking (unless done via the animation player for some reason).

Ah I think I get what you are trying to do and what your problem is.

If I understand you correctly, you are trying quite an advanced use case, which is teleporting while retaining movement, which is used for origin shifting.

I did previously add some functionality for this, but there may not be any on `SceneTreeFTI`, so you would have to do it manually currently.

The problem is this (if I understand what you are having issue with):
You are trying to move _both_ the current and previous xform to a new location.

To do this manually at the moment you would need to know your movement vector M (curr - prev).
You want to move to a new location B.

So you need to first move to B - M, call `reset` then set position to B. This should ideally be done on a physics tick.

I've done this sort of thing in origin shifting demos (I used it in this demo a while back https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aZRBgmNey_U ).
It's possible I can add a function to make this a lot easier (we previously didn't have much demand).

Let me know if this is what you meant, and I can mark it as feature request.

That sounds about right, I am retaining the movement of sorts in the teleport function (it converts the velocity in one of the functions) but the streaking on the weapon node does seem to stop if I let it inherit the parent transform or don't reset physics interpolation on the parent body. I've tried so many things the last few days and nothing seems to stop the streak once that function is called, as if it just totally overrides something internal that can't be changed manually. I also tried to defer the calls, yield some frames, etc, and whatever I tried the weapons node still streaks as it tried to come back to the player.

It seemed to stop if I do the weapon positioning in `physics_process`, but that causes permanent visual jitter, obviously, as the manual interpolation doesn't work correctly when manually positioning outside of `process`.

Ok I'll take a look at adding a function for origin shifting (I think I did previously have one added for the `VisualServer` approach, but didn't add one initially for `SceneTreeFTI`). It's usually pretty simple to add, and prevents the user having to worry about keeping track of the movement vector.

For more of the specifics you are mentioning, I suspect this might need reducing the MRP further, as it's kind of hard to work out exactly what you mean (it is probably obvious to you, but you may not see the forest for the trees as you are more familiar with the project).

Also bear in mind when it comes to games (as opposed to engine bugs), sometimes there are not "hard rules" of how you should structure things, they can work well in different ways with different trade offs.

I've made a simplified version that I've attached: [brokeninterpolation2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22583911/brokeninterpolation2.zip) The camera: has Physics Interpolation on: and has toplevel on: CamLerpPos is the position marker that the camera lerps to: and that has Physics Interpolation turned off (moves with the player, so toplevel is off too): Finally, the weapon node is attached to the camera: and has Physics Interpolation off: I don't have toplevel on that as it didn't make any difference. The camera lerps to the position marker: ```swift var tr : Transform = cam_lerp_pos.get_global_transform_interpolated() camera_target_position = lerp(camera_target_position, tr.origin, max(0.15,delta * global_vel_len * stairs_feeling_coefficient * camera_coefficient)) cam.translation = tr.origin ``` The weapons node then lerps to the camera (position and rotation): ```swift var tr : Transform = cam.get_global_transform_interpolated() weap_objs.global_translation = tr.origin weap_objs.global_transform.basis = tr.basis ``` Then the player teleports back a unit if it hits the area: ```swift onready var other_teleporter_node = self func _on_Area_body_entered(body): teleport(body) func teleport_position(teleporter1: Spatial, teleporter2: Spatial, pos: Vector3) -> Vector3: return teleporter2.global_transform.translated(global_transform.basis.z) * teleporter1.global_transform.inverse() * pos func teleport_direction(teleporter1: Spatial, teleporter2: Spatial, dir: Vector3) -> Vector3: return teleporter2.global_transform.basis * teleporter1.global_transform.basis.inverse() * dir func teleport_basis(teleporter1: Spatial, teleporter2: Spatial, bas: Basis) -> Basis: return teleporter2.global_transform.basis * teleporter1.global_transform.basis.inverse() * bas func teleport(body): body.global_translation = teleport_position(self, other_teleporter_node, body.global_translation) body.cam.global_translation = teleport_position(self, other_teleporter_node, body.cam.global_translation) body.cam.global_transform.basis = teleport_basis(self, other_teleporter_node, body.cam.global_transform.basis) body.rot_velocity = teleport_direction(self, other_teleporter_node, body.rot_velocity) body.reset_physics_interpolation() ``` (If I swap the physics interpolation on CamLerpPos marker and Camera (on CamLerpPos, off Camera), it works the same until I teleport, in which case the Camera streaks instead of the weapon node.) Now, I did have the weapons node just move with the camera and not interpolate manually, however I wanted to rotate the weapon based on how much up/down the camera is rotated: ```swift var frust_weap_z = -frust_val.y * 10 var frust_weap_y = frust_val.y * 10 weap_objs.translate_object_local(Vector3(0,frust_weap_y,0)) weap_objs.translate_object_local(Vector3(0,0,frust_weap_z)) ``` And if I do that on an interpolated node, it streaks and stutters whenever I rotate it that way. I cannot reset the physics interpolation with `weap_objs.reset_physics_interpolation()` as it streaks and stutters the entire time as it's inheriting the movement from the player camera (which is interpolated). So I had to manually add all of the interpolation to the weapons node so that all of it could be correctly interpolated. Except it breaks teleporting, as there's now two parts that are being interpolated and reset. PS: I found this on reddit: Unfortunately I couldn't use this as 3.x doesn't have `translated_local` and I don't know how to reimplement it myself, but theoretically I might be able to restore the weapons node as inheriting from the camera and just use this to do the local extra movement, but I'm still not sure if this would work and I'd like to find a way to get the node to not streak when its parent is reset anyways.

I realize this kind of thing can be difficult - creating e.g. a first person controller is non-obvious, and adding physics interpolation into the mix can make it confusing, hence we are trying to make some demos.

Your project seems to have a number of problems, and you appear to be throwing a complex project (rather than an MRP) into an issue, and saying "why doesn't this work?".

Just to be clear - this isn't really what contributors use github for.

Github issues are really intended for engine *bug reports*, rather than for general help with how to make a project, or for debugging user projects. The reason for this is that it just isn't practical for engine devs to debug users projects. We have limited time available and can't practically do this - we would have to do it again and again for every user.

What we try to do instead is write docs and create demos, so hundreds of users can learn from this instead of just one, and users can help each other (if they work out how to do something).

If you have a look at the physics interpolation docs, I did try to emphasize many times that the way to get things working is to set your physics tick rate to a low value (e.g. 10tps) and then you can see what is going right, and what is going wrong.

https://docs.godotengine.org/en/3.6/tutorials/physics/interpolation/physics_interpolation_quick_start_guide.html
https://docs.godotengine.org/en/3.6/tutorials/physics/interpolation/using_physics_interpolation.html#testing-and-debugging-tips

When I do this for your project and set TPS to 10, I can see that the weapon is totally out of sync with the camera, so something is going badly wrong.

I would advise starting fresh in order to build a working version, going in stages, and making sure you get each stage working, and understand why it works (or doesn't work) before moving on to the next stage.

(1) Fixed camera, have a player (e.g. a box) able to be moved by input with physics interpolation, and running smoothly at 10tps. Move the player and everything on the physics tick.

(2) Add a rig (using e.g. a Spatial) to the player so that you can e.g. rotate with the mouse in realtime, but still inherit the physics interpolated position. In Godot 3.6 / 4.5 (which have `SceneTreeFTI`) you can set this rig to `physics_interpolation_mode` OFF and it will inherit from the parent smooth positions, and you can directly set e.g. the rotation on each frame in response to input.

(3) Once (2) is working you can attach a camera and maybe a weapon, or weapon via IK to this rig.
